chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would lash the free man, the slave, the Jew, and the Christian regarding wine and Al-Nabeez with eighty (lashes). So I said, 'What is the matter with the Jew and the Christian?' He said: 'When they display that in a city from the cities, because it is not for them that they should be displaying their drinking of it.'
ai.seo_question: Why are Jews and Christians lashed for drinking wine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s application of the standard eighty-lash hadd to non-Muslims (Ahl al-Kitab) residing in Islamic lands, specifically linking their liability to the public nature of their consumption. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the principle that while Jews and Christians are exempt from the hadd when drinking privately, their public display of wine consumption in Muslim cities (amsar) subjects them to the same penalty as Muslims, reflecting the social order of the Islamic state. This distinction emphasizes the visibility of the act as a key determinant for the enforcement of the hadd in public spaces.
